title: Tanzanian Cowpea Leaves
community: Popular across Tanzania — both leaves and beans eaten
author: Mama Salima
desc: Tanzanian Kunde — tender young cowpea leaves sautéed with onions, tomatoes, and garlic. The protein-rich green that complements the cowpea bean — Tanzania's whole-plant vegetable where nothing is wasted.
longDesc: Kunde refers to both the cowpea plant's leaves (the vegetable dish) and its beans. The leaves are harvested young and tender and cooked like mchicha — the taste is slightly more earthy and nutty than amaranth, with a higher protein content.
ingredients: 400g young cowpea leaves — washed and chopped
steps: Heat oil. Cook onions until golden.
Add garlic and curry powder. Stir 30 seconds.
Add kunde leaves. Stir to combine.
Cover and cook 5—6 minutes until wilted and tender.
chefTips: Young leaves only — mature leaves are tough.
cookingScience: Cowpea leaves contain more protein than most leafy greens — approximately 5g per 100g cooked. The slight bitterness of raw cowpea leaves is reduced by brief cooking, which also increases iron bioavailability.
sustainabilityTips: The cowpea plant provides both leaves and protein-rich beans — maximum yield per plant.
healthBenefits: High protein for a leafy green.
culturalNote: Kunde leaves represent Tanzania's whole-plant philosophy — in Tanzanian cooking, every part of the cowpea plant is eaten and valued.
